entities.name: Benzyl-protected phenol substrate
observations: Contains an aryl benzyl ether, Ar–O–CH2Ph.

entities.name: Deprotected phenol product
observations: The benzyl protecting group is absent and the aryl oxygen is protonated as a phenol.

entities.name: Aryl O-debenzylation
observations: Net transformation is Ar–O–CH2Ph to Ar–OH; the cyclic acetal/ester core remains unchanged.
The database match lists ethyl acetate but does not explicitly identify the catalyst or hydrogen source.

entities.name: H2/Pd-C hydrogenolysis
observations: Most plausible reagent system for this aryl benzyl ether cleavage is hydrogen gas with palladium on carbon, commonly in ethyl acetate, ethanol, or methanol.

entities.name: Transfer hydrogenation debenzylation
observations: Plausible alternatives include Pd/C with ammonium formate or cyclohexene as a hydrogen donor when gaseous hydrogen is not used.
